A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Neighbor GRPO study and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary material. The relocated appendices and renumbered references can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original image-generation experiments, training-cost measurements, parameter ablations and a 46-participant human preference study.

after.justification: The original experiments in Tables 1–6, training curves, human evaluation and supplementary qualitative results are retained.

M1.justification: Neighbor GRPO's noise perturbation, surrogate policy, anchor-conditioned objective in Eq. 9, quasi-norm reweighting and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The preliminary GRPO formula correction does not document a changed proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same HPDv2 text-to-image training and evaluation coverage and human preference study. Neither adds video generation or scarce/noisy-reward experiments.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Table 1 includes FLUX.1-dev, DanceGRPO, MixGRPO and MixGRPO-Flash; Tables 2–3 retain their comparisons including BranchGRPO.

E3.justification: Both retain the 4800/9600 training prompts, 3200-prompt test set, 300 training iterations, reward and evaluation metrics, solver configurations, anchor settings and 46-user evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The perturbation-strength, anchor-count and quasi-norm ablations in Tables 4–6 are unchanged. Reward-hacking illustrations, rollout-diversity examples and supplementary qualitative comparisons are also retained.

E5.justification: Both report point scores, training curves and human preference percentages without experimental repeat counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain their numerical entries, and the training curves and qualitative images are unchanged. Figure 7 still reports 72% wins against MixGRPO and 61% against DanceGRPO. Removing the overbar on Table 3's 8 does not change its numerical value.

T1.justification: Equation 4 changes the KL term from +βDkl to −βDkl, correcting its direction in the maximized GRPO objective. The supplementary derivations are retained; their renumbering and residual-subscript adjustment introduce no new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and main conclusions retain the same claims about contrastive interpretation, SDE-free Neighbor GRPO, compatibility with high-order solvers and improved efficiency and generation quality.

C2.justification: The conclusion removes the outlook arguing that the method is particularly suitable for video synthesis and might offer robustness with scarce or noisy rewards. This narrows the discussion of prospective applicability; interpretations of existing results remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Optimizer settings, learning rate, GPU counts, H800 hardware, training time, solver details and pseudocode are retained. Moving Algorithm 1 into the supplementary section adds no implementation or resource-access information.

R1.justification: v2 removes the introduction citation and reference for Shen et al., 'Adt: Tuning diffusion models with adversarial supervision' (v1 reference 30). The remaining related-work discussion and positioning against SDE-based GRPO are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 updates an affiliation, adds contact emails and an acknowledgement, removes the future-work paragraph, and places references before a separately titled supplementary section. Most scientific prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 move from page 6 to page 7, and the algorithm and supplementary image grid are repositioned. Appendix Figure 9 becomes supplementary Figure 1. Table 4's caption is corrected from p normalization to perturbation strength; the underlying displays and data are retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting the KL sign in Eq. 4 and the misleading Table 4 caption improves mathematical accuracy and presentation clarity. Separating references from supplementary material also improves organization. The removed outlook was speculative, while the method and empirical evidence remain intact, so the overall improvement is limited.
